purpose: Component verification and external-model agreement for single-lane car trajectories and protected junction flow. Provisional study-specific criteria; no general urban-traffic accuracy claim.
timeUnits: seconds for physical inputs and metrics; runtime ticks remain integers

convergence.claim: Report measured trends; do not assume monotone convergence for every metric.

acceptanceCriteria.scope: Provisional numerical-equivalence targets for these matched-model experiments; separate from regression invariants and empirical validity.
acceptanceCriteria.headwayDefinition: Consecutive first-road exit event times within the same green interval; report count and match by vehicle pair.
acceptanceCriteria.queueDefinition: Vehicles on the approach with speed below 0.1 m/s, sampled at equal times; this is the halted queue, not every vehicle slowed by congestion.

stochasticReplications.stochasticSource: Independent seeded demand headway perturbations, shared exactly by both simulators; driver dynamics remain deterministic.
stochasticReplications.inferenceUnit: Scenario realization, not vehicles or time samples.
stochasticReplications.pairedMeanCi: Student t interval over independent per-seed HTC-minus-SUMO scenario means; n=5 uses t(4)=2.776445105.

empiricalValidation.requirement: Use documented units, quality-control continuity and lane changes, separate initialization/calibration prefixes from prediction intervals, retain raw query/hash/license, and state environmental applicability. Field availability alone does not establish validation.

reportingRules: Retain every held-out result, including failures. Never widen thresholds after execution without a new protocol version and fresh validation set.
Freeze parameters before held-out execution. Store protocol SHA256 in each result.
Report signed bias, absolute error, distributions, coverage and invariant checks; do not align traces by fitted time shifts.
SUMO agreement does not substitute for empirical validation. Stochastic demand intervals do not quantify all epistemic uncertainty.
Separate wall-clock failures and unsupported scenarios from physical acceptance; retain and label all exclusions.
